activity.internal_title: B1 | Grammar + Vocabulary | Future Arrangements and Changing Plans
activity.learner_title: Plans change: talk about arrangements naturally
activity.description: A mixed B1 lesson on scheduling language and forming present-continuous questions/statements for fixed future arrangements.
activity.instructions: Learn key scheduling vocabulary, notice how the present continuous is formed for fixed future arrangements, then use the language in realistic tasks.

blocks.title: Tomorrow is already busy
blocks.body: Nina and Paolo talk about fixed arrangements and a change of plan.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: I'm meeting the client at 3 tomorrow. The appointment is already confirmed.

turns.speaker: Paolo
turns.text: I'm calling the supplier in the morning.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Actually, I may need to reschedule my client meeting. Something came up.

turns.speaker: Paolo
turns.text: Are you moving it to Friday?

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Maybe. I'm checking their availability now.

turns.speaker: Paolo
turns.text: Let me know when the new arrangement is confirmed.

blocks.title: Core scheduling vocabulary
blocks.body: Learn these words directly. You will reuse them in the grammar and communication tasks that follow.

items.meaning: an arranged time to meet someone
items.example: I have a dentist's appointment at 11.

items.meaning: a plan organised with another person
items.example: Our travel arrangements are already fixed.

items.meaning: free and able to do something at a particular time
items.example: Are you available on Thursday afternoon?

items.meaning: arrange something for a different time or date
items.example: We need to reschedule the meeting.

items.meaning: move something to a later time or date
items.example: They postponed the launch until Monday.

items.meaning: decide that a planned event will not happen
items.example: We had to cancel the appointment.

items.meaning: say or show that an arrangement is definite
items.example: Can you confirm the time by this evening?

items.meaning: the latest time or date by which something must be completed
items.example: The deadline is Friday at 5 p.m.

items.meaning: able or willing to change according to the situation
items.example: I'm flexible about the meeting time.

items.meaning: causing difficulty or not suitable for someone's plans
items.example: Nine o'clock is a little inconvenient for me.

blocks.title: Talking about an arrangement
blocks.body: When a future meeting or appointment has already been arranged, English often uses the present continuous: am/is/are + -ing. The same form also needs normal present-continuous word order.

blocks.title: The arrangement pattern
blocks.body: Statement: subject + am/is/are + verb-ing. Question: question word + am/is/are + subject + verb-ing?
examples: We are meeting the client at 3 tomorrow.
What time are you meeting Sara on Friday?
Is Luca joining us for lunch?

blocks.title: Statement vs question
blocks.left_body: You are meeting the client at 3.
blocks.right_body: What time are you meeting the client?
blocks.body: In questions, move am/is/are before the subject. Keep the -ing form of the main verb.

blocks.title: Build the arrangement correctly
blocks.prompt: Choose the sentence with the correct present-continuous form or word order.
blocks.instructions: Focus on the structure used for fixed future arrangements.
blocks.learning_objective: Form statements and questions with the present continuous for future arrangements.

items.prompt: You and Marta have a fixed meeting tomorrow at 9. Which sentence is correctly formed?

options.text: Marta and I are meeting at 9 tomorrow.
Marta and I meeting at 9 tomorrow.
Marta and I are meet at 9 tomorrow.

items.prompt: Ask Luca about the time of his arranged call with Anna.

options.text: What time is Luca calling Anna?
What time Luca is calling Anna?
What time is calling Luca Anna?

items.feedback: In a question, put is before the subject: is Luca calling.

items.prompt: Ask your colleague whether she is joining the arranged lunch.

options.text: Are you joining us for lunch?
You are joining us for lunch?
Are you join us for lunch?

items.feedback: Yes/no questions use are + subject + verb-ing.

items.prompt: The client appointment is fixed for Friday. Which sentence is correctly formed?

options.text: We are seeing the client on Friday.
We seeing the client on Friday.
We are see the client on Friday.

items.feedback: Use are + seeing for the arranged future event.

blocks.title: Useful language when an arrangement changes
blocks.body: Use these expressions to explain the problem and suggest a new arrangement.
items: I'm afraid I can't make it at 3.
Could we move it to Friday?
Could we reschedule for next week?

blocks.title: Use the arrangement form in a real message
blocks.prompt: Complete the message with the correct present-continuous forms.
blocks.learning_objective: Retrieve be + -ing forms for arranged future events.
blocks.text_template: I [[blank_1]] the client at 3 tomorrow, and we [[blank_2]] the final details. What time [[blank_3]] you [[blank_4]] Marta afterwards?

blocks.title: Retrieve the scheduling words
blocks.instructions: Use the target vocabulary from the lesson.
blocks.learning_objective: Retrieve core scheduling vocabulary in short realistic sentences.

accepted_answers: I need to reschedule the appointment.
I have to reschedule the appointment.
items.feedback: Reschedule = arrange it for a different time.

accepted_answers: Are you available on Friday afternoon?
items.feedback: Available means free and able to do something at that time.

accepted_answers: Can we confirm the time tomorrow?
Could we confirm the time tomorrow?

items.prompt: La scadenza è stata posticipata a lunedì.
accepted_answers: The deadline was postponed until Monday.
The deadline has been postponed until Monday.
items.feedback: Postpone means move something to a later time or date.

blocks.title: Build the arrangement question
blocks.instructions: Build a natural question about a fixed future arrangement.
blocks.learning_objective: Form a present-continuous question about an arrangement.

blocks.title: Choose what you want in your vocabulary bank
blocks.prompt: Which words and expressions would be useful for your own work or daily life?
blocks.instructions: Select as many as you genuinely want to remember.
blocks.learning_objective: Select useful target vocabulary and chunks for later review.

blocks.title: Change the plan
blocks.prompt: Write a short message to a colleague. Refer to the fixed arrangement you need to change, explain the problem briefly, and suggest a new time.
blocks.instructions: Write naturally. Use the target grammar and some of the scheduling vocabulary, but do not force every item into the message.
blocks.learning_objective: Use scheduling vocabulary and accurate present-continuous arrangement forms in a realistic message.
blocks.context_situation: You are meeting a colleague tomorrow at 3 p.m., but something unexpected has happened and you cannot attend then.
blocks.context_role: You are the person who needs to change the arrangement.
blocks.context_audience: A colleague you know but still speak to professionally.
blocks.context_goal: Refer to the fixed arrangement, explain that it must change, and propose another time.
required_points: Explain briefly that it must change
Suggest a new day or time
Use at least two useful scheduling words or expressions
